blocks.body:
## Decision

The current Rust/WGPU all-resident path is **not a 40-step performance-and-accuracy pass** against PyTorch/CUDA on this 12 GiB GPU. WGPU won 0 of 18 condition medians and 0 of 90 paired fresh sessions. Its median condition-level readback penalty was 11.83%. Accuracy passed the hard gate in 14/18 conditions and the target in 9/18. Therefore earlier 4-step wins remain diagnostic results, not product-path performance claims.

## PyTorch remains faster across every measured length and voice topology

The smallest WGPU readback penalty was 3.00% at 333f · Text-only; the largest was 31.10% at 45f · Voice design. All 90 process-level pairs favored PyTorch, so the conclusion is not caused by one aggregated outlier. Device-complete and readback-complete are retained separately in the evidence; the chart uses readback-complete for both runtimes.

## Four conditions fail the 80 dB numerical hard gate

Hard failures are 333f · Prepared clone, 489f · Prepared clone, 489f · Voice design, 685f · Prepared clone. The worst is 489f · Voice design at 70.99 dB, max_abs 0.0019463, cosine 0.9999999602. Five more conditions pass hard accuracy but miss the 85 dB / 2e-4 target: 112f · Prepared clone, 255f · Prepared clone, 333f · Text-only, 489f · Text-only, 685f · Voice design. No auditory preference test was run, so these are numerical reproducibility results rather than claims of audible degradation.

## All-resident fits 12 GiB, but WGPU retains and peaks higher

The maximum WGPU NVML peak was 8822 MiB, leaving 3405 MiB below the reported 12227 MiB physical total. Python peaked at 6964 MiB. Allocator-internal persistent use was about 4798.7 MiB for WGPU versus 3448.5 MiB allocated by PyTorch, a 1350.2 MiB difference. This proves feasibility on this device, not portability to other adapters.

## Load and fresh-process warmup are separate from steady latency

Median model/codec load wall was 4.122 s for Python and 5.036 s for WGPU. One fresh campaign-local CubeCL environment and driver cache were primed, then imported into every WGPU session. Compute pipelines remained process-local and were rebuilt after each launch; the first request is stored separately from the 10-request steady median. This campaign does not report external launch-to-WAV-close cold E2E, because each process performs two warmup requests before its measured set.

## Methodology and semantic-work contract

Both runtimes used strict FP32, TF32/autocast off, 40 Euler evaluations, independent CFG, text/caption/speaker scales 3/4/5, CFG window 0.5–1.0, linear schedule, fixed shared FP32 noise, and no tail trim or watermark. The 41 schedule bits match exactly. Text-only uses 60 effective rows; design and prepared clone use 80. Each request performs 40 whole-model forwards, 12 layers, and 480 block calls. The runtimes do the same semantic work, not the same operator graph.

## Limitations

This is one NVIDIA/Vulkan/CUDA laptop GPU and one pinned driver. Durations are exact fixed frame counts, so duration prediction is excluded. Clone uses prepared references; raw reference encoding is measured only in preparation and excluded from online latency. Fixed noise is necessary for numerical comparison but does not reproduce an official sample's random seed, automatic duration, or every request input. NVML is device-level memory used under an exclusive GPU lock, not a per-allocation trace.

## Recommended next work

1. Stop performance adoption and localize the first numerical divergence for 333/489/685-frame clone and 489-frame design, preserving the 80 dB hard / 85 dB target split.
2. Profile the 40-step RF path at the matched schedule; the product-path gap compounds across 40 forwards, so codec-only wins cannot offset it.
3. Reduce prepared-weight residency only after verifying every required shape has a valid fallback-free route; the present all-resident path costs about 1.35 GiB more internal live memory than PyTorch.
4. Run a separate cold external-process and duration-prediction campaign; do not mix it with this steady all-resident estimator.

## Reproduction and pins

Use source commit `8a19782fd3e22017abf04b475c903c058a017af2`, model revision `e4aaac4df355ff560dcd35e0dae272c3a759317b`, codec revision `47376ee24834d7a05a48ebabfe3cde29b3c5e214`, GPU `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU`, driver `595.71.05`, PCI `00000000:01:00.0`, CUDA/NVML index 0, and WGPU adapter 0. The SHA256SUMS file digest is `b5fe310825d3eeaf2b19a2a17460a9c8678c8a94bbc606e11589c9332485ecd3` and covers 1,723 files. Run `scripts/run_v4_40step_formal_compare.sh --output-dir <fresh-path>`; existing paths are rejected and automatic retries are disabled.

charts.question: Does WGPU overtake PyTorch at any practical output length or voice topology?
charts.rationale: A scatter preserves all 18 condition estimates and exposes length scaling without treating the six lengths as a time series.
charts.subtitle: WGPU minus PyTorch, percent; 18 condition medians, each from five fresh processes × 10 measured requests. Positive favors PyTorch.
charts.title: Readback-complete latency delta by output duration

charts.question: Which practical shapes cross the numerical accuracy thresholds?
charts.rationale: All 18 condition-level SNR values remain visible against both declared gates.
charts.subtitle: Rust/WGPU output versus PyTorch/CUDA with identical FP32 noise and sampler bits; 80 dB hard gate and 85 dB target.
charts.title: Waveform SNR by output duration

charts.question: Does the all-resident configuration fit the 12 GiB device across all measured lengths?
charts.rationale: Two lines show the conservative per-length peak envelope for each runtime.
charts.subtitle: Maximum across three voice conditions and five fresh sessions at each length; one benchmark process held the GPU lock.
charts.title: NVML peak VRAM by output duration

manifest.description: Fresh PyTorch/CUDA versus Rust/WGPU all-resident performance, accuracy, memory, load, and warmup evidence on a 12 GiB GPU.

query.description: Validated condition and session aggregates generated from sealed raw Python, WGPU, wall-clock, audio, and NVML evidence.
filters: strict FP32; TF32 and autocast disabled
40 Euler evaluations; linear schedule; independent CFG
2 warmups plus 10 measured requests per fresh process
fixed shared FP32 initial noise; tail trim and watermark disabled
no automatic retry and no sample pooling from older campaigns
metric_definitions: Condition latency is the median of 10 measured requests within each process, then the median of five fresh-process medians.
Readback-complete ends after an owned contiguous CPU F32 waveform exists for both runtimes.
Hard accuracy requires finite output, waveform SNR at least 80 dB, and cosine at least 0.99999999.
Target accuracy additionally requires SNR at least 85 dB and max absolute error at most 2e-4.
NVML peak is 100 ms device memory.used sampling while the benchmark holds the GPU lock; it is not allocator-internal memory.
